project.name: The Lantern at Low Tide

sources.name: acceptance.md
sources.content:
- Scene stays in Mira’s close third-person perspective, between 17:40 and 18:00.
- Established lantern, ferry and character-knowledge constraints are respected.
- Draft is 800–1200 words; count and method are stated.
- Continuity report cites source filenames/sections and distinguishes canon, inference and proposal.
- No new canon is silently inserted; unresolved conflicts become owner questions.

sources.name: world-bible.md
sources.content:
# World bible
## Setting
Tern Quay is a fictional tidal harbor. The footpath to the lighthouse floods at 18:10.
## Lantern rule
The blue lantern is bolted inside the tower and cannot be carried away. It shines only while seawater touches its copper basin. No portable duplicate exists in established canon.
## Timeline
17:40 Mira reaches the harbor steps. 18:00 the last ferry departs. 18:10 the footpath floods.
## Tone
Quiet wonder, concrete coastal details, no graphic violence. Technology is hand-built and mechanical; no phones or electricity.

sources.name: characters.md
sources.content:
# Characters
## Mira
Apprentice tidekeeper, age 24. Observant and impatient with ceremony. Wants to warn the ferry captain. Knows the basin rule but does not know who loosened the drain valve.
## Oren
Retired keeper, age 61. Knows the valve was deliberately loosened, but has not told Mira. Remains in the tower during this scene.
## Captain Vale
Waits at the ferry until 18:00. Has never seen the basin. Do not give Mira access to Oren’s private knowledge without a scene event.

sources.name: scene-brief.md
sources.content:
# Scene brief
Close third-person through Mira, 17:40–18:00. She must decide whether to miss the last ferry to warn Oren that the lantern is flickering. End with a consequential decision, not the mystery solved. Use the harbor, tower and receding tide. The outline in starter/ is a prompt, not completed prose.

requirements: Cohandry 0.1.13 or later and your own supported model connection.
A connected text-capable model; no execution host is required for a text-only draft.
A word-count tool is optional; label a model-only count as unverified. No art or paid assets are required.
